claims.claim: Python's lexical analyzer turns decoded source text into tokens before parsing; source that cannot be decoded raises SyntaxError.
A logical line can be made from one or more physical lines according to explicit or implicit line-joining rules.
A comment starts with a hash outside a string literal, ends at the physical line's end, and is ignored by syntax.
Leading whitespace on a logical line determines grouping, and inconsistent tab/space indentation that depends on tab width raises TabError.
A compound statement has clauses with headers and suites; a suite is a group of statements controlled by a clause and the header ends with a colon.
A simple statement occupies one logical line, while multiple simple statements can be separated by semicolons on that line.
